newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl urges German SPD to rejoin tax talks.
newsitem.headline: Kohl urges German SPD to rejoin tax talks.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl on Friday repeated his call to the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) to rejoin cross-party talks on tax reforms which they broke off a week ago in a clash over coal subsidies.
"The government has made its offer. The SPD has to do the rest," Kohl said before a meeting of his Christian Democrats (CDU) called to agree a pensions reform policy.
Kohl said he was still waiting for the SPD to offer constructive proposals. "Apart from a barrage of criticism, we have heard very little from the other side," he said.
Kohl on Thursday cleared up the coal dispute, but the two sides sparred in public on Friday over whether to resume talks on Finance Minister Theo Waigel's plan to cut 30 billion marks in taxes.
He said that the SPD was faced by the question of whether it should "fulfil its duty to Germany or just criticise".
Kohl also said that he would seek a political consensus on reforms to Germany's pay-as-you-go pensions system.
The CDU was due to discuss alternative pensions schemes.

One, drafted by Labour Minister Norbert Bluem, would keep the current system intact while winding down old-age pay to 64 percent of average net wages in 2030 from 70 percent now to take account of the demographic ageing of Germans.
The other is a tax-financed model put together by Saxony state premier Kurt Biedenkopf.

CDU officials have said that the Bluem plan is likely to prevail, and Kohl said he would introduce legislation into parliament as normal rather than holding pre-legislation talks with the opposition as he has done on taxes.
The CDU will hold a mini-party conference next Wednesday to finalise its position on pensions.
